rule: GOAL: Pick up the red, green, and blue pieces in the order shown to build the chain. CONTROLS: Up and down moved the head along the rail. Right extended the arm; left pulled it back. RULE: Touching a piece attached it, and pulling back carried attached pieces with the arm. TRAP: Thinking the striped arm was a trailing body hid how reaching and pulling worked.

GOAL: Get the blue piece to the blue outline while a replay holds the switch that opens the red gate. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the piece along corridors. Space started the other run and replayed the first; using it again reset both. RULE: A piece on the switch opened the gate, so one run could clear the way for the other. TRAP: Thinking Space would remove the red barrier wasted time; the switch controlled it.

GOAL: Reach the target by using a recorded run to hold a switch and open the way. CONTROLS: Arrows moved your piece. Space started another run while a ghost replayed your earlier moves. RULE: A piece on a switch moved its linked barrier; the ghost could keep the route open. TRAP: Treating the red barrier as something Space would remove wasted time. Its switch controlled it.

GOAL: Guide the craft through the blocked corridor to the pink marker. CONTROLS: Left and right moved the craft sideways. Clicking a green block removed it without moving the craft. RULE: Open a lane, then steer into it to make the route advance automatically. TRAP: Removing all the green blocks did not finish the level; the craft still had to travel through the openings.

GOAL: Use recorded runs to open the barriers, then reach the goal with the final piece. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the piece. Space saved a run and started the next; after the last slot, it reset the runs. RULE: Ghosts replayed earlier moves. Red barriers needed a piece holding their switch; yellow stayed open after its switch was left. TRAP: Thinking Space always kept useful recordings cost time; cycling past the last slot erased them.

GOAL: Collect red, orange, blue, then green in that order. CONTROLS: Up and down moved the arm along the rail. Right extended it; left retracted it, carrying collected pieces. RULE: The rod tip collected pieces. Moving the arm vertically pushed loose pieces; carried pieces could also push them. TRAP: I thought orange touching the carried red would attach it. Orange only joined when the rod tip reached it.

GOAL: Reach the exit by leaving ghosts on the red and purple switches, then using the open corridor and portal. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the active piece. Space saved its route and started another run while ghosts replayed saved routes. RULE: A ghost could hold a switch while the active piece went elsewhere; reach the portal after both ghosts reached their switches. TRAP: Assuming every arrow press moved the piece wasted a recording: a blocked step left the ghost short of its switch.

GOAL: Guide the craft past barriers to the pink marker. CONTROLS: Arrows steered the craft; clicks removed green blocks. The craft rose automatically through open space. RULE: Blocks could be brakes as well as barriers: leave some overhead to stop at a safe turn. TRAP: Clearing every block looked helpful, but let the craft rise into a deadly purple and yellow structure.

GOAL: Collect red, orange, blue, then green on the horizontal rod. CONTROLS: Right extended the rod, left retracted it, and up and down moved it vertically. RULE: Pieces on the vertical support had to slide off its bottom before the rod could carry them away. TRAP: A lit goal mark did not mean a piece was secured. Retracting too soon left it on the support.

GOAL: Open the yellow gates, leave ghosts holding the red and purple switches, then use the portal to reach the goal. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the piece; Space saved a nonempty route for a ghost to replay on the next run. RULE: Yellow gates stayed open; red gates and portals needed held switches. Only successful moves advanced ghost replays. TRAP: Pushing against a wall seemed like waiting, but it did not advance the ghosts. Step away and back instead.

GOAL: Guide the craft to the pink goal, opening a safe path around purple hazards. CONTROLS: Arrows steered the craft. Clicks removed green blocks or switched orange tiles between solid and open. RULE: The craft rose automatically until blocked; solid orange tiles could act as brakes, while open cross marks were safe to cross. TRAP: Thinking an orange cross mark was dangerous led to clicking it again and closing the path.

GOAL: Stack blue above green on the cyan support, and red above orange on the yellow support. CONTROLS: Up and down raised and lowered the rod and threaded pieces. Right extended the rod; left withdrew it. RULE: Supports let pieces stay parked while the rod was withdrawn, so groups could be separated and stacked. TRAP: Assuming every withdrawal dragged every threaded piece left. Extending through a piece did

GOAL: Leave recorded ghosts on the red switches, reach the bottom switch, then return to the goal before moves ran out. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the active piece and advanced the patrol. RULE: The patrol shifted the yellow gates; cross through the spaces they left open. TRAP: A switch’s yellow connecting line looked like a corridor, but it was not walkable. The return trip used the timed crossings again.

GOAL: Put the pieces into the required arrangement while working around the fixed obstacle. CONTROLS: Up and down moved the rod vertically. Left pulled it back; right extended it. RULE: The rod could retract completely, leaving every piece behind, so carrying a piece was not always necessary. TRAP: Assuming the rod had to hold at least one piece ruled out useful moves and wasted time.

GOAL: Guide the craft to the pink target without touching purple hazards. CONTROLS: Movement steered the craft sideways. Clicking green blocks removed them; activating red tiles reversed gravity. The staircase carried the craft upward. RULE: Gravity pulled the craft until a solid block stopped it, so intact floors and ceilings provided safe stopping places. TRAP: Flipping gravity near the open entrance seemed safe, but sent the craft into purple hazards. Activate from beneath an intact ceiling instead.

GOAL: Guide the craft to the pink target without touching purple hazards. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the craft sideways. Clicks reversed gravity at red switches, removed green blocks, or made orange outlines solid. RULE: Gravity carried the craft until a solid block stopped it; keeping or adding blocks made safe stopping places. TRAP: Assuming orange controls removed hazards wasted time. They created blocks that could stop the craft before it hit a hazard.

GOAL: Reach the exit by changing gravity and preparing safe landing blocks. CONTROLS: Arrows moved you; red switches reversed gravity; orange outlines could be filled or cleared to make or remove blocks. RULE: Solid blocks stopped falls, but empty outlines did not. Purple surfaces were deadly, so landing blocks had to be ready before reversing gravity. TRAP: Blaming the budget for deaths wasted time; the real cause was falling through unfilled outlines onto purple floors.

GOAL: Line up the green and yellow sliders’ red tips with their target markers. CONTROLS: Each colored arrow panel moved its matching slider: green sideways, yellow up or down. RULE: Movement came in fixed steps; the green right button extended its bar by three spaces. TRAP: Assuming each click moved just one space led to the wrong move count.

GOAL: Guide the linked arm through the gap above the purple wall and line up its red tip with the target. CONTROLS: Colored arrow buttons extended matching segments: orange and yellow right, sky blue up, green down. RULE: Each click extended a segment by three spaces and moved the pieces attached beyond it. TRAP: Treating the colored pieces as separate sliders hid how an early extension shifted the whole arm.

GOAL: Move both target bars onto their red markers by clearing the barriers from their paths. CONTROLS: Red lowered a white barrier; orange shifted another right. Blue moved the red assembly left; green lifted the orange assembly. The target bars’ buttons extended their tips. RULE: Attached barriers moved with their supporting bars, and blocked moves were refused. TRAP: Believing nearby colored bars were linked wasted moves; red and orange actually moved the white barriers.

GOAL: Raise the central yellow tip to its target while keeping the side bars clear. CONTROLS: Yellow extended or retracted all five yellow bars together. The colored controls raised or lowered the side bars. RULE: Shared movement meant every yellow bar needed clearance, not just the central one. TRAP: Treating yellow as a control for only the central tip hid why the side bars needed repositioning first.

GOAL: Guide the green and sky blue tips onto their targets while clearing the walls and moving barrier. CONTROLS: Orange raised or lowered the green tip; green moved it sideways and lifted the barrier; blue shifted the barrier sideways; sky blue extended or retracted its bar. RULE: Linked pieces moved together, and a collision could stop the whole move. TRAP: Trying to advance green while sky blue stayed extended. Retracting sky blue first made room for the barrier to rise.

GOAL: Guide the arm’s tip to the target beneath the purple overhang, using the gap on the left. CONTROLS: Colored panels extended or retracted matching segments. Buttons above them rotated the arm’s joints. RULE: Moving a segment also moved the pieces attached to it, so the whole arm needed clearance. TRAP: Trying to reach straight down wasted time; the overhang required a route around its left side.

GOAL: Sort the colored beads into the required color groups. CONTROLS: Click a rod to make it active. Arrow keys move it sideways or extend and retract it. RULE: Beads on the other rod are pinned, and beads cannot be pushed onto that rod. A blocked sideways push stops the whole move. TRAP: Assuming every blocked bead stops extension too. An extending rod can pass through a blocked bead without moving it.
GOAL: Put both blues and green on pink’s rod, and both reds and green on purple’s rod. CONTROLS: Click a rod to select it; use arrows to move

GOAL: Guide the colored arm ends onto their matching targets while fitting through narrow gaps. CONTROLS: Extension panels lengthened or shortened sections. Rotation buttons turned sections and everything beyond them. The red control turned the red barrier. RULE: A turn moves the whole attached chain, so shorten folded sections before moving through tight spaces. TRAP: Treating the red barrier as fixed wasted time searching for a route around it.

GOAL: Move the purple block along the dotted route to the blue circle. CONTROLS: Click the white cross to move the block onto it, then click farther along the route. RULE: Use the marked stopping point instead of trying to jump straight to the goal. TRAP: Clicking the blue circle or the purple block itself would start movement; neither did.

GOAL: Guide the green marker to the yellow target by arranging a connected path. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the marker two spaces; the red button turned the red bridge; the blue button switched which blue bridge was solid. RULE: Only solid, connected bridges could carry the marker. TRAP: Assuming the blue button rotated the whole mechanism instead of switching bridge states.

GOAL: Merge the small pieces into a final block and move it into the blue goal. CONTROLS: Click nearby spots to move pieces toward them; clicking the goal alone does nothing. RULE: Matching pieces merge into the next color when they meet, but clicks have limited reach. TRAP: Assuming a click between two blocks would pull both together; it moved only the nearer one.

GOAL: Guide the green marker to the yellow target by connecting the bridges. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the marker two spaces. Red turned its bridge; blue switched which blue crossing was solid. The small floor control needed a visit, not a click. RULE: Cross solid bridges, and stand on a fixed pivot when turning a bridge beneath you. TRAP: Assuming every colored control worked remotely wasted time; the small red control had to be reached on foot.

GOAL: Make one yellow block and one purple block, then deliver each to its own blue goal. CONTROLS: Click near pieces to draw them toward the click; move blocks with short steps. RULE: Matching pieces merge into the next color: cyan, magenta, purple, then yellow. Keep one purple aside. TRAP: Believing a distant goal click would pull a block all the way there wasted clicks; movement had limited reach.

GOAL: Guide the green marker to yellow using bridges, pink pads, and the purple route. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the marker two spaces. Red rotated its bridge; blue switched solid crossings; pink teleported between pads; purple activated purple paths after unlocking. RULE: Only solid paths supported movement. Collecting a colored token unlocked its control, and fixed bridge pivots were safe places to rotate. TRAP: Thinking blue rotated a bridge wasted time; it switched which crossings were solid.

GOAL: Combine all eight cyan pieces into one yellow piece and place it in the goal. CONTROLS: Clicking pulled nearby pieces toward that spot. Reset restored the starting layout. RULE: Matching colors merged: cyan into magenta, magenta into purple, purple into yellow. The pink hazard moved after clicks and weakened pieces it reached. TRAP: Treating the pink symbol as harmless wasted a run. Save the exposed pieces first and merge away from it.

GOAL: Reach the exit by crossing the upper bridge, using the moving platforms, and restoring the lower bridge. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the marker. Yellow shifted both platforms right, then back left. Gray extended one bridge while shortening the other. Pink pads teleported between each other. RULE: Platforms did not carry the marker, and changes that would leave it unsupported were refused. Walk between safe shifts. TRAP: Assuming the platform would carry you when it moved wasted time.

GOAL: Merge matching blocks into the goal block while keeping enough material safe from hazards. CONTROLS: Clicks moved and merged blocks; reset restarted the level. The color swatches were a legend, not controls. RULE: Hazards pursued blocks, not empty clicks, and their attacks downgraded blocks. TRAP: Trying to lure hazards away by clicking empty space wasted turns while they attacked the blocks.

GOAL: Turn the red block yellow, then place yellow and pink in separate goals. CONTROLS: Click to pull nearby pieces toward that spot. Reset restarts the level. Color swatches are only a legend. RULE: Pink contact lowered red to orange, then yellow. Pink also moved toward colored blocks. TRAP: Believing clicks repelled pink wasted time; the final test showed nearby pieces were pulled toward the click.

GOAL: Reach yellow by collecting the purple token, moving bridges, and using the pink teleport pads. CONTROLS: Arrows moved you; small arrow buttons moved the claw; red gripped or released orange; colored buttons switched paths; gray moved the small platform. RULE: The claw followed the white rail. Stand directly on pink to teleport, and use the small platform to switch safely between purple paths. TRAP: Thinking the white rail was walkable wasted time; it carried the claw, not you.

GOAL: Fill both goals with yellow blocks, using merges for one and pink splitter contacts for the other. CONTROLS: Click to pull nearby blocks and pink splitters toward the click. Reset starts the level over. RULE: Merging blocks raises their color; splitter contact lowers it. Red becomes orange, then yellow. TRAP: Thinking clicks pushed pink away wasted moves. Pink follows nearby clicks too, and the color swatches are only a legend.

GOAL: Put two orange pieces and one green piece on goals. CONTROLS: Click near movable pieces to steer them. Faraway clicks and legend swatches did nothing. RULE: Two yellows merged into orange; two pinks merged into green. Pink contact lowered red to orange, but could lower orange again. TRAP: I thought green came from pink touching a block. It actually came from merging two pinks.

ESTABLISHED: Two rows of five switches can change; the yellow objects stayed fixed. The level remains uncleared. FAILED: Visiting every switch setting and testing blue center clicks across multiple settings produced no clear. GOAL IS NOT: Simply cycling through all switch settings. No winning condition has been confirmed. CONTROLS: Each switch toggled its own bit. Blue center clicks had no visible effect. The reset control’s effect

GOAL: Move the orange and blue block onto the white cross. CONTROLS: The arrow keys moved the block in five-cell steps in the chosen direction. RULE: The block moved while the white cross stayed fixed, marking the target. TRAP: Assuming the blue-symbol chamber was the exit wasted moves; it blocked entry.

GOAL: Turn the carried symbol to match the exit, then reach it before the move bar ran out. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the block one step; entering the cross turned its symbol a quarter turn. RULE: Three cross entries gave the needed match. Yellow rings refilled the move bar; keep each stretch within about twenty-one moves. TRAP: Treating yellow rings as teleporters wasted time. They refilled the bar without moving the block.

GOAL: Reach the exit with the symbol matching its color and direction before the move budget runs out. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the block through passages and onto special tiles. RULE: The multicolor tile changed color, the cross turned the symbol, and yellow tiles restored the budget once each. White-edged passages carried the block straight to their far ends. TRAP: Thinking a used yellow tile would refill the budget again wasted a return trip.

GOAL: Reach the exit with the carried symbol matching its color and shape before moves run out. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the block; stepping onto special tiles changed the symbol, refilled moves, or triggered transport. RULE: Color tiles cycled colors, the white transformation tile changed shape, and white edge strips transported away from the strip along its row or column. TRAP: Assuming every white strip sent the block downward led to loops and wasted moves.

GOAL: Bring the exit a matching red zigzag with an extra detached square before moves run out. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the block; special tiles changed its symbol, refilled moves, or transported it. RULE: The rotation cross followed a four-step cycle, advancing only when the block moved successfully. TRAP: Treating the cross as fixed made a planned pair of visits produce only one rotation.

GOAL: Guide the craft through the upper opening, down the outer shaft, and onto the goal without hitting hazards. CONTROLS: Side controls moved the craft left or right; red reversed gravity; orange placed a brake. RULE: Gravity carried the craft until a ledge or brake stopped it, so brake height determined which passage it could enter. TRAP: Mistaking camera scrolls for moving terrain hid the true connections between passages.

GOAL: Reach the red destination, then the blue one, carrying the matching shape and facing each time. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the block. Shape tiles changed its form, turn tiles rotated it, and refill tiles restored the move budget. RULE: There were six shape families, and changing form kept the current facing. TRAP: Assuming only five forms, or assuming a shape change reset its facing, led to wrong predictions and wasted moves.

GOAL: Guide the craft into the goal chamber by crossing its roof and opening the entrance. CONTROLS: Click blocks to change the path, click the red switch to reverse gravity, and use arrows to move sideways. RULE: Gravity keeps carrying the craft until a solid block stops it, so build a landing before reversing. TRAP: Reversing gravity does not stop the craft at the goal; without a landing, it falls past the entrance.

(unreviewed excerpt) World model: Standing on the top switch retracts the red gate from the left corridor. The recording now ends on that switch. I’ll use Space to start the second run, which should let the replay hold the gate open.

GOAL: Collect the loose pieces to build the red, green, blue chain shown below. CONTROLS: Up and down moved the head along the rail; right extended the rod and left pulled it back. RULE: A piece joined the rod when touched, then moved with it; the target marks showed progress. TRAP: Treating the bottom chain as a control wasted time. It showed the goal, not something to press.

GOAL: Guide the craft through the winding passage to the pink goal. CONTROLS: Left and right arrows moved the craft sideways. Clicking a green block removed it. RULE: The craft rose on its own whenever the space above was clear, stopping beneath the next obstacle. TRAP: Thinking sideways movement alone would solve the route wasted time; green blocks overhead had to be clicked away.

GOAL: Get the blue piece to the blue outline beyond the gate. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the piece; Space returned it to the start for a new run while replaying the first route. RULE: A piece on the red switch opened the linked gate, so the replay could hold it open for you. TRAP: Thinking two switches and three runs were needed; one recorded route and one new run were enough.

GOAL: Reach the blue outline by recording two routes that leave replays holding the red switches. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved your piece. Space ended a recording, returned you to the start, and began the next run alongside earlier replays. RULE: Red gates needed their switches held down; the yellow gate stayed open after its switch was released. TRAP: Assuming the yellow switch also needed a replay parked on it wasted a run.

GOAL: Guide the rising craft to the goal through green blocks, avoiding purple-and-yellow hazards. CONTROLS: Steering moved the craft sideways. Clicking a green block removed it. RULE: The craft rose whenever its path was clear; intact green blocks acted as brakes. TRAP: Believing every overhead block should be removed. Some had to stay so the craft could stop safely and move sideways.

GOAL: Record one run to hold the red switch and another to hold the purple switch, then reach the goal through the rings. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the piece. Space returned it to the start for a new run while earlier runs replayed. RULE: Replays could hold switches, but needed time to reach them before the final run used the opened route. TRAP: The middle looked like a crossing, but was blocked; reaching the purple switch required going around the top.

GOAL: Guide the craft to the pink goal without hitting hazards. CONTROLS: Arrows steer the craft; clicks remove green blocks or switch orange tiles between solid blocks and open crosses. RULE: The craft rises through open space until a solid block stops it. Restored orange blocks can act as brakes. TRAP: Thinking every block should be cleared. Removing a needed brake can send the craft up into danger.

GOAL: Attach the beads in order: red, orange, blue, then green. CONTROLS: Up and down moved the arm; right extended it; left retracted it. Reset restarted the level. RULE: The tip collected beads, while the shaft could push loose beads aside. The white marks showed the correct starting sequence, not every bead collected. TRAP: Collecting all four was not enough. Attaching green before blue made the chain wrong, and clicking could not detach it.

GOAL: Record routes to purple and red, then use the clear central route and teleport to reach the goal before moves ran out. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the piece. Space cleared recordings but did not refill the move bar. RULE: Yellow switches toggled gates on every visit, including visits by replays, so recording order mattered. TRAP: I treated yellow as a switch that simply opened a gate; repeated replay visits closed the route again.

GOAL: Thread the colored beads onto the horizontal rod in the required order. CONTROLS: Up and down moved the rod vertically; right extended it and left pulled it back. RULE: Beads slid off the rack at its lower end. Loose beads needed the far wall behind them before the tip could pass through them. TRAP: Touching a bead did not mean it was collected; pulling back too soon left it behind.

GOAL: Guide the craft into the goal chamber without hitting hazards. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the craft sideways; clicking green blocks removed them, while clicking red controls reversed its vertical pull. RULE: The craft moved with the pull until a block stopped it, so intact green blocks could serve as brakes. TRAP: Reversing in an open lane seemed safe, but it sent the craft too far upward; keeping a green brake overhead made the route work.

GOAL: Guide the craft around walls and hazards into the goal. CONTROLS: Arrows moved sideways. Clicking red reversed vertical travel. Clicking green removed a block; clicking its orange marker restored it. RULE: The craft kept rising or falling until a block stopped it, so blocks were brakes as well as barriers. TRAP: Thinking every green block should be removed. Some had to stay to stop the craft before hazards.

GOAL: Reach the goal by timing yellow gate crossings and taking the outer corridor to the bottom switch. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved your piece; successful moves also advanced green along its route. RULE: Green’s switch visits changed the gates, so safe crossings depended on move timing. TRAP: Pressing into a blocked gate did not advance green. Waiting that way could never bring the next opening.

GOAL: Guide the craft through the walls and hazards to the exit. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the craft sideways. Clicking orange markers toggled brakes; red controls reversed vertical travel. RULE: The craft kept rising or falling until blocked. Restored brakes made later crossings safe. TRAP: Believing a brake removed for the upward trip could stay absent on the return descent.

GOAL: Put blue above green on one rail and red above orange on the other. CONTROLS: Left and right changed the arm’s length and shifted beads on its row. Up and down moved the arm, carrying reachable beads and pushing others ahead. RULE: Rails blocked sideways entry, but beads could enter from below. A blocked bead could stop the whole move. TRAP: Assuming finished pairs would stay put; moving a long arm could drag them out again.

GOAL: Bring both colored bar tips to their cross marks. CONTROLS: The green arrows shortened or lengthened the sideways bar; the yellow arrows did the same for the upright bar. RULE: Each press moved a tip three spaces, so count in threes. TRAP: Expecting each press to move just one space led to wrong counts.

GOAL: Guide the four-color chain around the purple walls until its tip reaches the red cross. CONTROLS: Each button pair extended or retracted one segment: orange right, sky blue up, yellow right, and green down. RULE: Each press moved a segment by three spaces and carried every later segment with it. TRAP: Treating the colors as separate bars wasted time; changing an earlier segment also shifted the rest of the chain.

GOAL: Move the sky blue and pink tips onto both crosses by clearing their paths. CONTROLS: Each colored button pair extended or retracted its matching bar, carrying attached parts along. RULE: Moves were blocked by collisions, so the linked white barriers had to be moved in the right order. TRAP: Treating the white bars as fixed walls wasted time; they were movable barriers controlled by the colored bars.

GOAL: Bring the central yellow tip to the cross while keeping the four side bars clear of its path. CONTROLS: Yellow extended or retracted all five yellow bars together. The other colored controls moved their supports. RULE: Linked bars moved together, so the side bars needed safe lanes before the central tip could advance. TRAP: Treating the yellow tip as independent led to blocked moves; the side bars needed arranging first.

GOAL: Get the green and sky blue tips onto their crosses, routing green through the purple wall’s gap. CONTROLS: Colored controls extended or retracted matching bars; both green segments moved together, as did both orange supports. RULE: Linked pieces moved as a group, and solid obstacles blocked their movement. TRAP: Treating sky blue’s alignment as untouchable cost time; retracting it temporarily made room to route green.

GOAL: Bring each colored tip onto its matching cross, routing blue through the purple enclosure’s left opening. CONTROLS: Paired buttons extended or retracted their bars; upper colored buttons rotated linked segments. Support controls moved attached bars together. RULE: Plan around walls and linked movement: clear a path before extending, sliding, or turning an assembly. TRAP: Assuming a bar could move freely once its tip crossed a wall. The stretched bar could still catch on it; retract before repositioning.

GOAL: Guide the craft onto the pink goal while avoiding purple hazards. CONTROLS: Steering moved sideways, red controls reversed gravity, and brakes stopped the craft. RULE: A reversal could remove nearby red controls, so preserve one for the final turn. TRAP: Treating all reversal sites as equivalent left the last control out of reach.

GOAL: Collect red, blue, red on the shaft, in that order, before the move budget ran out. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the shaft; S detached beads. RULE: A loose bead could push another bead, letting you move reds past the wall while the shaft stayed above it. TRAP: Blaming retraction for a failed attempt; the move budget had simply run out.

GOAL: Bring each colored tip to its matching cross. CONTROLS: Extend and retract changed a segment’s length; turn swung that segment and the chain beyond it. RULE: Walls and the chain blocked moves, and turning skipped blocked directions. TRAP: Assuming every turn was a quarter turn led to bad plans; check the actual pose after each click.

GOAL: Move the purple block along the dotted route to the blue goal. CONTROLS: Click a nearby point to move the block there; each attempt uses some of the move bar. RULE: Moves have limited reach. Use short hops, with the white cross as the first waypoint. TRAP: Believing a distant click would make a longer move wasted the move bar without moving the block.
GOAL: Combine the eight sky-blue pieces into one yellow piece. CONTROLS: Click a

GOAL: Make one yellow piece and one purple piece, then place them in the two blue goals. CONTROLS: Click a nearby spot to move a piece there; bring matching pieces together to merge them. RULE: Two sky-blue pieces make magenta, two magenta make purple, and two purple make yellow. TRAP: A distant click does not move a piece, but still spends the move bar. Use short hops.

GOAL: Merge matching pieces into yellow, then bring yellow to the goal. CONTROLS: Clicks moved pieces in short hops and merged matching pieces. Clicking the pink pursuer did nothing. RULE: The pursuer moved after every click and weakened pieces it caught, so merges and movement had to keep

GOAL: Clear the level with two clicks, not a long search through switch settings. CONTROLS: Clicking switches flipped them; tested clicks on the board and handle did nothing. RULE: An empty action bar ended the attempt; a reset did not mean the last switch was dangerous. TRAP: Believing the right

GOAL: Guide the craft through the shaft and into the orange goal entrance without hitting hazards. CONTROLS: Click blocks to change the purple barriers, click red switches to reverse gravity, and use arrow keys to steer. RULE: Gravity carried the craft until something stopped it. Keeping a brake beneath it allowed a controlled descent after gravity reversed. TRAP: Assuming the red edge switches moved the camera wasted time; they changed gravity and could leave the craft trapped below the goal.

GOAL: Move the piece to the goal four spaces above its start. CONTROLS: Click switches to change command pairs, use the bottom icons to select command banks, run to execute, and reset to clear the program. RULE: Two black switches made an upward move; two gray switches did nothing. Four upward commands with the rest blank worked. TRAP: Assuming gray pairs moved downward wasted attempts and drained the action bar.

GOAL: Set the command pattern needed to pass through the wall’s central gap and reach the goal. CONTROLS: Direction icons selected example patterns; switches changed your pattern; execute tested it; reset cleared it and restored the budget. RULE: Use the left panel’s examples as the encoding guide instead of guessing what switch combinations mean. TRAP: Assuming gray switches meant unused commands wasted attempts; even apparently blank settings needed to match the examples.

GOAL: Merge the pieces into yellow before the move budget ran out, while protecting them from pursuers. CONTROLS: Click to move and merge pieces; reset starts the level over. RULE: Matching pieces combine into a higher color, but pursuers can downgrade them. TRAP: Thinking a pursuer that turned green was harmless. It could still downgrade a purple piece on later turns.

GOAL: Guide the piece to the goal by entering a safe sequence of moves. CONTROLS: Direction icons showed example codes; switches edited the program; run executed it; reset cleared it. RULE: Each column of six switches encoded one move. Copy the matching direction example from the left panel. TRAP: Treating pairs of switches as separate commands wasted clicks. Read the whole column as one code.

GOAL: Guide the piece down through the narrow gap, changing its size, orientation, and color to match the goal. CONTROLS: Icons showed command examples; switches entered them; run executed the sequence; reset cleared it. RULE: Each column of six switches encoded one whole command. Copy the examples, then arrange commands in order. TRAP: Treating switch pairs as separate movement commands wasted time; the full column mattered.

GOAL: Bring a yellow piece onto the blue goal. CONTROLS: Click to move the piece; the fixed pink mark was not a button. RULE: Reaching the goal was not enough—the piece had to match the required color. TRAP: Assuming the moving pink piece would turn orange into yellow led to wasted waiting and chasing.

GOAL: Get all three reds on purple and the blues on pink, matching both panels before the move budget ran out. CONTROLS: Click selected a handle; arrows moved it or extended and retracted its shaft. RULE: Shafts could cross, and a bead needed to sit well inside the tip to move with retraction. TRAP: Assuming a bead at the tip would retract with the shaft wasted moves.

GOAL: Fill both goals with yellow pieces. CONTROLS: Click to move pieces and merge matching ones. Reset starts the level over. RULE: Matching pieces merge into the next color; pursuers can lower their color as turns pass. TRAP: A long diagonal click did not move the yellow. Use shorter hops and deliver it before the pursuer catches it.

GOAL: Fill the three goals with two orange pieces and one green piece. CONTROLS: Clicking the board pulled nearby pieces toward the click and moved the pink chasers. Reset restarted the level. RULE: Matching pieces merged into the next color. Yellow pairs made orange, pink pairs made green, and a chaser could knock red down to orange. TRAP: I thought the color swatches selected pieces, but they were only a legend.

GOAL: Guide the green piece to the yellow marker. CONTROLS: Arrows moved green two cells. Clicking red rotated its bridge; clicking blue switched which blue bridge was solid. RULE: Solid bridges provided paths; checkered bridges did not. Safe landings let you change the route before crossing. TRAP: Assuming the arrows moved the whole frame wasted time; only the green piece moved.

GOAL: Guide the piece through the corridors, using checkerboard checkpoints to reach the finish. CONTROLS: Switches set the direction in each command slot; Run tried the batch. Blank slots left unused commands empty. RULE: Read this level’s direction key, and aim batches at checkpoints rather than assuming one batch must cover the whole route. TRAP: Reusing an earlier level’s direction codes made planned moves go wrong and confused the checkpoint tests.

GOAL: Guide green to yellow by using the rotating bridge, paired pink pads, and purple route. CONTROLS: Arrows moved green. Red rotated the bridge. Blue switched which gates were solid. Magenta teleported between pink pads. Purple activated its routes once unlocked. RULE: Floor symbols could unlock controls; a checkered route was not yet walkable. Set each connection before crossing. TRAP: I thought magenta would enable the purple paths. It actually teleported green, so the purple control still needed unlocking.

GOAL: Reach the exit by building bridges, crossing sliding platforms, and using the pink teleport pads. CONTROLS: Arrows moved you. Gray changed bridge lengths. Yellow shifted the white platforms sideways through a repeating cycle. Pink pads teleported you between landings. RULE: Platforms did not carry you, and a shift stopped if it would remove your floor. Walk and shift in turns. TRAP: Assuming you could stand still and ride a moving platform wasted time.

GOAL: Guide the blue and orange block through the gray corridors to the white target. CONTROLS: The arrow keys moved the block up, down, left, or right. RULE: Each move covered five cells, and the block could not enter dark walls. TRAP: Mistaking the white target for the moving piece wasted time; the colored block was what you controlled.

GOAL: Arrange the colored beads into the target pattern. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the shafts sideways or changed how far they reached. RULE: Extending changed reach without moving beads; sideways sweeps moved beads, while shortening pulled them only when unblocked. TRAP: Assuming an extending tip pushed beads led to plans that did not work.

GOAL: Turn the symbol to the required orientation, then reach the exit before energy runs out. CONTROLS: Arrow keys move the block. Entering a white marker turns the symbol; entering a yellow ring refills energy once. RULE: Every move costs energy, even a blocked move. Empty energy resets the board, so plan turns and refills together. TRAP: Trying to finish all three turns before recharging wasted attempts. Two turns, a refill, then the third turn left enough energy to continue.

GOAL: Reach the exit with the symbol matching its blue color and orientation before the move budget runs out. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the block; restart restored the board and both refills. RULE: White markers turned the symbol a quarter turn; multicolor tiles changed color without turning it. Yellow rings refilled the budget once, and pale edge strips teleported the block. TRAP: Treating pale strips as ordinary floor made route plans wrong and wasted moves.

GOAL: Reach yellow by collecting the purple unlock and connecting the platforms and bridges. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the green piece; colored controls shifted platforms, cycled the gray bridge, and switched purple paths. Pink pads teleported between landings. RULE: Purple paths alternated, so stand on the gray platform before switching from the vertical path to the horizontal one. TRAP: A partly extended gray bridge looked ready to cross. Check that both halves meet before stepping onto it.

GOAL: Reach the exit with the block’s color and shape matching its target before moves ran out. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the block; entering special tiles changed its color or shape, refilled moves, or teleported it. RULE: Match the exact shape pattern, not a rough outline. One shape change and three color changes gave the needed match. TRAP: Thinking the first shape change was wrong led to needless cycling; it already matched the exit.

GOAL: Make the required shape, rotate it to match, turn it red, and reach the goal before moves run out. CONTROLS: Arrows moved you; special tiles selected shapes, changed colors, rotated the symbol, or refilled moves. RULE: Preserve the finished symbol by avoiding shape controls, and use refills and verified portals to reach the goal. TRAP: Believing every corridor tip wrapped around wasted moves; the useful goal portal was at the bottom of the right passage.
